analysis: Only a test file changed (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift; new tests at head lines 3140-3239). No production code is in the supplied units, so no direct security regression is observable. The new tests cover SSDWholeRootMaintainer behavior in the T-041 retained cache area (TB-007): (1) header-ownership verdicts are remembered only for unchanged files, keyed by ctime as well as size and mtime, so a restored mtime cannot keep a stale ownership proof (lines 3140-3166); (2) a malformed lookalike replaced by a real block is re-read (3168-3191); (3) a header read that fails for reasons outside the file, such as EACCES, is retried and not cached as a negative verdict, so maintenance cannot be silently disabled (3193-3239). Existing tests in the surrounding context confirm the fail-closed behavior: lookalike files without DBK3 ownership proof are never deleted, symlinked ancestors are rejected (3241-3273), and temp cleanup requires an exact name match and age (3275-3332). Per-donation gate, queue-bound and sidecar tests (HMAC domain-separated window tags, a metadata AAD that carries only a keyed base commitment and never the raw position) are consistent with the T-041 posture that nothing prompt-derived beyond keyed tags goes to disk. Remaining question for the integrating pass: the production maintainer's verdict cache (not supplied) must key on the ctime/inode/size identity and must not cache transient read failures. These tests assert that but cannot prove it. This pass could not verify the production implementation, so coverage is limited to test intent.
